newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO's iron ore, scrap demand to rise.
newsitem.headline: POSCO's iron ore, scrap demand to rise.

text.p: South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd (POSCO) said on Tuesday its demand for iron ore, coal and steel scrap is expected to rise by 2000 because of an expansion in steel production capacity.

"Demand for iron ore is expected to rise by about four million tonnes to 38.1 million tonnes by 2000, when the Number Five Blast Furnace is in full operation, from current 34.1 million tonnes," Kang Koo-sun, managing director of POSCO told Metal Bulletin's Fourth Asian Steel Conference in Seoul.
The Number Five Blast Furnace is expected to have an annual production capacity of three million tonnes of crude steel and to be completed in 1999.

Kang said demand for lump and fine iron ore would remain at the current level of 8.5 million tonnes and 23.5 million tonnes respectively or increase slightly to 8.6 million tonnes and 24.7 million tonnes.
But iron ore pellet demand would more than double to 4.8 million tonnes a year from the present level of 2.1 million tonnes, Kang said.
"To meet our increasing demand for pellets, we began joint construction of a pellet plant with an annual production capacity of four million tonnes with the CVRD of Brazil," Kang said.

Kang said POSCO would consume half of the pellets produced from the joint-venture plant, which is expected to start operation from June 1998, and the rest of its requirements would be met by other suppliers.

Meanwhile, POSCO has been looking for further diversification of its coal supply sources among Australia, South Africa, China, Indonesia, the U.S. and Latin American countries as its coal demand is forecast to rise to 19.9 million tonnes by 2000 from a current 18.5 million tonnes, he said.

Hard coal demand is expected to fall by 400,000 tonnes to 12.5 million tonnes in 2000 from 12.9 million tonnes in 1996, while semi-soft coal may rise by 1.8 million tonnes to 7.4 million tonnes from 5.6 million tonnes, he said.
Last year, Australia supplied 9.1 million tonnes of coal to POSCO, Canada sold 4.2 million tonnes and the United States supplied 2.4 million tonnes in 1995.

When POSCO's expansion in steel mini-mills is completed, its demand for steel scrap and hot briquetted iron (metallics) in 2000 is expected to reach 29.4 million tonnes from 18.6 million tonnes in 1995, he said.

However, he expected a shortage of around 5.2 million tonnes of metallics in 2000 since POSCO's demand would outpace supply which expected to rise 24.2 million tonnes from 12.9 million tonnes in 1995.
To solve the expected shortage, POSCO has been proceeding with a hot briquetted iron joint-venture in Venezuela with an annual production of 1.5 million tonnes.
POSCO also expects it can secure a certain portion of the hot metal from the Number Five Blast Furnace to use as a feedstock for the mini-mills.

After recently completing the construction of a mini-mill with an annual crude steel production capacity of 1.8 million tonnes, POSCO is planning to build a second mini-mill by 1999 with a steel production capacity of two million tonnes a year.
